title: Notify Transport for NSW that a customer has died
summary: Learn how to notify Transport for NSW (TfNSW) that a person with licences or vehicle/vessel registrations has died.
intro:
If a person with licences and/or vehicle or vessel registrations has died, you can advise Transport for NSW (TfNSW) by providing an appropriate document confirming the death.

The Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages does inform TfNSW of a death, but it can take some time.
who_can_apply: The person who died must have licences and/or vehicle or vessel registrations.
what_you_need: Letter from a solicitor or the NSW Trustee and Guardian advising that the person has died
A completed Advice of Death – PDF form
Proof of identity documents for the person who died and the person notifying of the death
For missing persons presumed deceased: 'Presumption of Death Order' issued by the Supreme Court (original or copy)

faqs.q: How do I notify TfNSW that someone has died?
faqs.a: You can notify TfNSW by providing an appropriate document confirming the death. You can submit this by emailing transactions.parkes@service.nsw.gov.au, posting to Service NSW, Parkes Middle Office, PO Box 21, Parkes NSW 2870, or visiting a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What documents are needed to notify TfNSW of a death?
faqs.a: You need documents such as a death certificate, newspaper death notice, online newspaper notification, or a letter from a solicitor or the NSW Trustee and Guardian.

faqs.q: What if the person is missing and presumed deceased?
faqs.a: If the person is missing and presumed deceased, you must provide a 'Presumption of Death Order' issued by the Supreme Court (original or copy). In this case, the Advice of Death form cannot be used.
